question: Who among the following was the key leader of the Khongjom War (1891) against British annexation of Manipur?

options.text: Tikendrajit Singh commanded the Manipuri army and was later executed.
Rani Gaidinliu led resistance against the British in Naga regions post-1930s.
U Kiang Nangbah led uprisings in Jaintia Hills against colonial intrusion.
Veer Surendra Sai resisted the British in Sambalpur for over four decades.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Tikendrajit Singh commanded the Manipuri army and was later executed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tikendrajit Singh**, also known as Senapati (General), was a key figure in the **Khongjom War of 1891**, which marked Manipur's resistance against British annexation.
 
• As the Commander of the Manipuri Army, Tikendrajit led the defense forces of Manipur in their fight against the British Empire.
 
• The war culminated in the Battle of Khongjom, where Manipuri forces faced overwhelming British forces but displayed exemplary valor.
 
• Following the defeat, Tikendrajit was arrested by the British and executed publicly on **13 August 1891**, becoming a martyr for India’s freedom struggle.
 
• The Khongjom War is commemorated annually in Manipur as **Khongjom Day** to honor the sacrifices of Manipuri warriors like Tikendrajit Singh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rani Gaidinliu**

 
 
• Rani Gaidinliu was a Naga spiritual and political leader who led resistance against British rule in the 1930s.
 
• She was associated with the Heraka religious movement, which sought to revive traditional Naga culture and religion.
 
• She was arrested by the British in 1932 and sentenced to life imprisonment but was released after India’s independence in 1947.
 
• She was honored with the title of **‘Rani’** by Jawaharlal Nehru for her role in the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **U Kiang Nangbah**
 
 
• U Kiang Nangbah was a freedom fighter from the Jaintia Hills (present-day Meghalaya) who led a rebellion against British colonial rule in the 1860s.
 
• He opposed the imposition of taxes and the erosion of traditional Khasi-Jaintia governance by the British.
 
• Captured by the British, he was executed in 1862, becoming a symbol of resistance in the region.
 
 
 
• **Veer Surendra Sai**
 
 
• Veer Surendra Sai was a prominent freedom fighter from Odisha who led resistance against British rule in Sambalpur for over four decades.
 
• He fought against the annexation of Sambalpur under British policies and defended tribal rights and local governance.
 
• His prolonged resistance lasted until his capture in 1864; he was imprisoned for the rest of his life.
 
 
 
• **The Khongjom War (1891)**
 
 
• The Khongjom War was the last war of independence fought by the Kingdom of Manipur against British annexation.
 
• Despite the advanced weaponry of the British, the Manipuri soldiers fought bravely to protect their sovereignty.
 
• It marks a significant chapter in India’s freedom struggle, highlighting the resilience of smaller kingdoms against colonial powers.
